pages.title: Shell: the window and its rail
pages.note: Superseded by 0.3 Atlas shell; kept for the record. The frame every view sits in: the brand, the views, what is coming from the KIV and the Observatory, the four ways to speak to everyone, and the portal's state at the foot. It matters because it is what Kris sees first and last: the portal line answers "are both Macs here?" on every page.
fields: Brand: the meeting ring, "Agora", which Mac this is
Views: Home, Who's doing what, What's being said, Broadcasts, Waits on you, Macs and the portal, Checkouts, each with a count where one helps
Later: Inbox (from the KIV), Insight (from the Observatory), shown but not yet live
Speak to everyone: Broadcast…, Away… (I'm back while away), Ping, Mark all
The portal: the two Macs and whether the portal is open, with when the other was last heard
Tabs: Home first, then each page or document opened, closable

pages.title: Shell: the tray
pages.note: The menu-bar menu, the quiet everyday face of Agora (DESIGN-2). The app opens from its first line. It matters because most days Kris only ever sees this: two lines must say whether all is well.
fields: Line 1: agents and Macs heard from
Line 2: All well, or how many need a look
Exception rows: at most 3, each with what Agora saw, what it did, at most two actions
Speak to everyone
Detail one level down: Agents, Macs and checkouts, Runs, Broadcasts, News
Agora itself: Sync now, Open log, About, Quit

pages.title: Atlas shell (sidebar superseded by 0.4)
pages.note: Its sidebar is superseded by 0.4 Atlas shell, revised (Kris's review, 22:55 to 23:20 GMT): Home leaves the sidebar for the logo, the map becomes Known Lands under Work, and every place sits in a section with a small eyebrow. The toolbar, tabs, context control, tray and bottom pane here still stand; the boards are kept, drawn in the 0.3 sidebar, for the record. The frame every page of Agora Atlas sits in, now that the app holds far more than the first pack drew: the map, the work (Roadmap, Jobs), the guilds, the Observatory's instruments, the KIV's pages, accounts, settings and updates. It replaces the rail of 0.1. It matters because each page so far brought its own tray, pane and filters; one shell with fixed places for navigation, context, detail and documents lets Kris learn the window once, and lets the Roadmap, Jobs and Guilds designers build on the same frame (atlas_page in build/mocks.py; IA.md has the rules).
fields: Toolbar (N1): Agora Atlas, the rigs, one word on the whole, the search, Mark all, Away…, Broadcast…, the time, pin and theme
Sidebar groups (N2): Agora, Work, Guilds, Observatory, KIV (folded while it is coming), Coming; a count only where something waits
Sidebar foot (N3): Accounts, Settings, Updates; the portal between the rigs; Beacon in the menu bar and Lantern on the iPhone
Tabs (N4): the place or document in each tab; a sidebar click replaces the current tab, ⌘-click opens a new one
Context (C1), top right: the territory and the plane for every page that reads them; greyed, not hidden, where a page ignores one
Page (P): the page header and its content, which the page owns
Right tray (T1): the facts of one selected thing; it pushes the page narrower and closes with × or Escape
Bottom pane (B1): the selected thing's documents or long readings, in tabs; drag its top edge to resize

pages.title: Atlas shell, revised
pages.note: Kris's review (22:55 to 23:20 GMT) of the 0.3 sidebar. Home leaves the sidebar and is reached by clicking the Agora Atlas logo, as on a website; the map that was Home becomes Known Lands, under Work, with an old chart for its glyph. Every place now sits in a section with a smaller eyebrow, every section folds, and folded to icons each section keeps a three-letter eyebrow: AGO, WRK, GLD, OBS, KIV, SYS. Accounts, Settings and Updates form SYS at the foot, above the portal line. It matters because the sidebar is on every page: one rule for every section is quicker to learn than groups, a lone place and a foot that each behaved differently. Every page in the pack now draws this sidebar, except 0.1's and 0.3's own boards.
fields: Logo (N5): Agora Atlas in the toolbar is Home; it is underlined while Home is open, and says "Home" on hover
Sections (N2): AGO Agora, WRK Work (Known Lands, Roadmap, Jobs, Art gallery later), GLD Guilds, OBS Observatory, KIV (folded while it is coming)
Eyebrow: 9.5-point capitals with a fold chevron; folded, it carries its count of places and, in a gold-edged word, what inside wants a look
Folded to icons (⌘\): the three-letter eyebrow heads each section; a folded section is a dashed box with its letters and a chevron
Foot (N3): SYS (Accounts, Settings, Updates), then the portal between the rigs, Beacon and Lantern
Known Lands: a curled chart with a dotted path to an X, so it reads as a map and not as a graph

pages.title: Atlas bar, compact
pages.note: Kris's review (23:05 GMT) of the toolbar: it took too much room, the sol and terra chips would not hold ten rigs, counts such as "2 must settle" said nothing on hover, and At a glance was unclear and popped out. The bar is now one 36-point row. The rigs are one presence control, its mark the worst state among them, opening a list of every rig; they show as chips only while three or fewer fit. The counts are one notification indicator, its count and worst state as a mark and a word, leading to Home's Needs a look (9.1), where each item says what it is and what to do. At a glance is gone: its contents are on Home. Every control has a tooltip in words. It also settles one rule for the right tray and every pop-out (IA.md, Pinned and floating): the tray pins, a pop-out floats. It matters because the bar is on every page and must still read when the group grows.
fields: Bar (N1): window lights, sidebar, the logo (Home), presence, Find, the notification indicator, speak to everyone, the time, pin, theme; 36 points
Presence (N6): up to three rigs as chips, each a shape and its name; more as one control, "10 rigs", the worst mark and its word ("1 gone"), opening the list
Notification indicator (N7): a bell, the worst mark (✓ nothing, ◆ look, ▲ urgent) and its words ("Nothing", "3 to look at", "4 · 1 urgent"); click for Home's Needs a look
Speak to everyone (N8): Mark all, Away… and Broadcast… as three icon buttons, each with its tooltip
Tooltips: on every control, words only, after a short pause or on keyboard focus; never an action
Right tray (T1) pins: it opens on a chosen thing, pushes the page, and stays until × or Escape
Pop-out (T2) floats: it opens from its control over the page, never pushes, and closes on Escape, a click outside, a choice, or its control again

pages.title: Known Lands (was Home)
pages.note: Known Lands since 0.4: the map that was Home now sits under Work, and Home (9.1) is reached from the logo. One view that fits the window with no scrolling (MSG-62774774, Kris's vision): the territories and their islands, the work packages and workers placed where they work, the primary focus of each, the island portal on each island, the threads of talk up to each territory's principal portal and across, and the planar portal, on its own island ki-portal, between the planes. The preferred home (1f) makes it a working map: active islands stand out, Focused hides the quiet ones, each island carries its queued work and waiting messages, and clicking an island shows its detail in the right tray. It matters because it is the page the app opens on, and it should show the whole distributed Agora as one place where Kris can see where work is and pick it up.
fields: Toolbar: Focused or Everything; the plane (sol, terra or both); zoom out, the level, zoom in, Fit; Show as a list
Territories, each a faint boundary with its name
Islands (repositories), drawn as hexes: active as land, quiet as outlines
On each island: its name, queued work (a stack) and waiting messages (an envelope), each a small count; zero left out
Island portal on each island: lit when someone there listens; the principal portal larger on each principal island
The planar portal on ki-portal in Personal, ringed in gold, kept by the watchman; sol and terra, open or not
Workers by role: council, enabler, doer; each with its primary focus and rig
Listening by shape: solid listening, hollow on open, slashed silent
Threads of talk: island portals up to the principal portal, principal portals across, the planar portal out to the other plane
Right tray, an island selected: where it is, its portal, checkouts, who works there, queued work, waiting messages, what waits on Kris
Right tray, nothing selected: at a glance and the key
Zoomed: labels stay at reading size and add when each worker last answered; an overview shows where the view sits

pages.title: Who's doing what
pages.note: Every live agent on both Macs, what each looks after, whether it listens, and what waits on Kris; and the address book for routing by focus. It matters because routing an idea to the right agent depends on it, and because listening is shown from answers, not from what an agent says of itself.
fields: Agent: work id and title
Mac (as the group row)
Territory
Focus areas, primary first (★)
Listening: how (Agora's call, polling, on open, off) and last answer
Waits on you: count and first ids

pages.title: An agent
pages.note: One agent closer up: its focus areas with what each covers, its listening over the last two hours, the run and doers with it now, what was said with it, and its queries. It matters when an agent goes silent or holds many queries: everything needed to act is on one page.
fields: Focus areas with descriptions
Listening: method, recent answers, next check
With it now: run, doers, checkouts
Said with it: last hour, both directions
Waits on you: query, what, focus, since, recommended answer

pages.title: What's being said
pages.note: Everything said between agents and to Kris on both Macs, newest first, in both layers. It matters because "everyone hears" is Agora's first goal: this is where Kris sees what was said and whether it was heard. It is a record to look along, not a chat.
fields: Time
From → to
Kind: message, call, broadcast, ping, mark, health, pushed
Layer: Git (durable) or Agora (conversational)
What was said, in a line
Heard: when, or silent

pages.title: Broadcasts
pages.note: What Kris said to everyone, and who heard it. It matters because a broadcast such as Away opens an unattended window: Kris needs to know every agent took it.
fields: Sent
What
Kind: message, away, back, ping, mark
Heard: answered of reached
Silent: who did not answer
For the selected one: each agent, answered or silent

pages.title: Waits on you
pages.note: Every query waiting on Kris across all agents, gathered in one place. It matters because these are the decisions only Kris can make, and today they sit in ten separate discussions files.
fields: Query id
What, in a line
Focus
Since
Recommended answer
Agent

pages.title: Macs and the portal
pages.note: The two Macs and the portal between them: presence, where each listens, its Agora, agents and checkouts, and what crossed the portal this hour. It matters when something is not getting across.
fields: Per Mac: presence, address, Agora version and uptime, agents, checkouts, last review
The portal: network, last heard and round trip, traffic this hour, queued, state swapped

pages.title: Checkouts
pages.note: Every kept checkout on both Macs, side by side, showing only those not level by default. It matters because "everyone is level" is Agora's second goal, and a diverged checkout blocks an agent.
fields: Repository
Condition on sol
Condition on terra
Whether the Macs agree
For the selected one: what Agora did and who was called

pages.title: A document in a tab
pages.note: Pages and documents open inside the app as tabs, as in Orca and Claude Code, so a message, a decision or a record can be read beside the map without bringing in the KIV's and the Observatory's views first.
fields: Tabs: Home stays first; each opened page or document after it, closable
The document, read only, with where it lives and when it changed
About this document: its package, how Agora uses it, where it was opened from

pages.title: Roadmap
pages.note: Every work record on the lands this Mac carries, read from each island's docs/roadmap/ or a knowledge base's Streams/Roadmap/ front matter, as the built app reads it (src/app/roadmap.ts). Kris asked for "the roadmap table ... filter it based on the summary table ... and on different factors", with the details in the right-hand tray. It matters because the records are spread over a dozen islands: this is the one place to see what is in progress, what waits for review and what is piling up in triage, and to pick one up. It settles the summary-filter bar (7.1.1) that Jobs shares.
fields: Tallies (P2): All open, then each open status (in progress, awaiting review, ready, draft, triage) with its count; a click keeps only that status, ⌘-click adds one; done and cancelled are one tally, hidden until chosen
Chips (P2): the territory from the context first, then each chosen value, removable; one Filter menu for priority, horizon, area, size, island, kind and assignee, each value with its count
Words to find in an id or title; Group by status, island, area or none
Records (P3): id, title, island, status (mark and word), priority and size, when it last changed; a long group folds after a few rows
Right tray (T1), a record chosen: its front matter, what it is blocked by and blocks, its Goal and Context; Open the file, Read in full (the bottom pane), Show on Home

pages.title: Jobs
pages.note: Every scheduled job and service Rig declares on either Mac, grouped by the territory and then the repository each one works in, as the built app does (src/app/jobs.ts). Kris asked for "a similar list view ... based on the scheduled jobs, by territory, and then by repository". It matters because a job that fails at 07:15 on one Mac is otherwise noticed only when its output is missed. Agora only shows: running, starting or stopping a job stays Rig's (KI-AGORA-WRK-004).
fields: Tallies (P2): All, Failed, Findings, OK, No run yet, Off, Services; Failed and Findings carry the gold edge while non-zero
Chips (P2): territory and plane from the context; one Filter menu for kind, Mac, profile and provider; words; Group by repository, Mac or none
Jobs (P3): name and Rig id, schedule in words, each Mac that runs it marked by how its last run there ended, last run, next run by its schedule, how it stands

Right tray (T1), a job chosen: its standing, purpose, the declaration (id, schedule, next, declared, profiles, provider, label, works in, program), each Mac's last runs as marks and the last one's line; Show runs, Open its file, Show on Home
Bottom pane (B1), after Show runs: every run kept on both Macs, newest first: finished, Mac, outcome, summary; and the declaration
Never shown: a job's environment, arguments or output

pages.title: Guilds
pages.note: The guilds and their skills, read from each *-agentic-harness island on the lands, and a chosen skill's documents (src/app/guilds.ts, skills.ts). Kris asked for "each of the guilds ... some kind of panel with a logo on it, what the guild is about, and then underneath it a bank of skills". It matters because seventy-odd skills are only findable today by knowing their folder; the badges make the guilds a place to browse, and the pane reads a skill without leaving Atlas. The territory is the context control's. Until the guildmaster's catalogue (ki.reg.guilds) names the guilds, each harness folder stands in, and the page says so.
fields: Guild badges (P2), across: All guilds, then each guild's badge: its logo or monogram on its own colour, its name and how many skills; a badge is a tally, so choosing it keeps that guild
Skills (P3): the chosen guild's about line and its skills as sub-badges, each with its guild's small shield; with All guilds, a ledger, one guild a row
Words to find a skill by name, description or guild

Bottom pane (B1), a skill chosen: its guild and harness, its name, and a tab for SKILL.md (front matter, then its instructions drawn), each other document and each folder (references/, scripts/, assets/) with its files
Notices: provisional guilds; a harness without skills; another territory's own unsorted skills as one guild

pages.title: Home: who holds what
pages.note: Home, reached from the Agora Atlas logo (0.4). Kris's review asks for "who holds what": one row per live package with its role, tier, rig, focus areas and state, with a footnote wherever a package's record disagrees with the guild catalogue, and the roles the catalogue names that nobody holds yet. Needs a look sits above it, each item saying what it is and what to do, so the page Atlas opens on answers "is anything wrong, and who is on it?" first. It matters because the map shows where work is; Home shows who answers for it.
fields: Needs a look (P2): urgent or look, each a mark and a word; what it is; what to do; one plain action

Who holds what (P3): Role (Kris's emoji and its word), Tier (Leader, Manager, Doer), Package (the work id), Rig, Focus areas on one line (⭐ and bold for the primary, ⏰ for something scheduled), State (🤖 Working, 👤 With you, 💤 Idle, 🔕 Silent)
Doers appear as Doer rows, with the package that brought them in
Footnotes (P4): † ‡ § mark the cell where the record and the catalogue disagree; the row shows the catalogue
Yours to approve (P5): catalogue roles not yet created, with the proposed package and rig; the one brass action approves the section
Right tray (T1), a row chosen: its facts, its focus areas with their schedule, and the record beside the catalogue

artboards.why: Every place is one click away and stays where Kris learnt it, grouped by what it is about; the KIV, still coming, folds to one line so the sidebar fits without scrolling. Context, detail and documents each have one fixed place, so every page behaves the same.
artboards.gains: One look shows all of Atlas; counts in the sidebar say where something waits; the context control sets the territory once for Home, Roadmap, Jobs, Guilds and the Observatory; the tray and the bottom pane open the same way on every page.
artboards.costs: Twenty-odd places is a long list: with the KIV unfolded it needs folding elsewhere or a scroll; the sidebar takes 220 points (56 folded); a greyed context control on Settings or Guilds is one more thing to read past.

Sidebar folded: Home, the territory menu open
Tray and bottom pane together: Jobs, a job and its runs
Sections across the top: Work, Roadmap, a record in the tray
artboards.gains: The sidebar holds only the section's few pages, so it never needs folding or scrolling and leaves more of the window to the page; the five sections name the app's parts plainly; it grows by adding a section.
artboards.costs: Crossing sections (Roadmap to Home, Jobs to Guilds) takes two clicks and the sidebar changes under the pointer; counts in other sections are out of sight; Accounts, Settings and Updates hide behind the gear; the toolbar is fuller.

artboards.title: Sidebar in sections: Known Lands under Work, KIV folded
artboards.why: One rule for every section: an eyebrow, a fold, its places. Home is where Kris expects it, on the logo, so the sidebar holds only places to go; Known Lands sits with the other work it leads to, and the foot is a section like the rest.
artboards.gains: The sidebar is shorter by one row and reads as six named parts; folding works the same everywhere; folded to icons, the three-letter eyebrows keep the parts apart; SYS makes Accounts, Settings and Updates foldable like the rest.
artboards.costs: Home is one more thing to learn for someone who expects it first in the list; the logo must say "Home" on hover (0.4c); Guilds has an eyebrow over a single place, which repeats its name.

Compact bar: two rigs as chips, 3 to look at, the indicator's tooltip

artboards.gains: 12 points back for the page on every screen; the bar never grows with the group; one place to look for anything that wants a look, and one click to Home's list; no count without words.
artboards.costs: Mark all, Away… and Broadcast… lose their words to icons (their tooltips carry them); a third rig's chip must fold before a fourth can; one more click to see which rig is gone.

artboards.costs: 48 points tall; ten rigs do not fit; "2 must settle" says nothing on hover and leads nowhere; a second count would need a second word.

artboards.title: The working map: Focused, an island selected
artboards.why: It keeps the picture Kris described and makes it the place to act from: Focused shows only where work is, each island says how much is queued and waiting, and one click opens an island in the tray without leaving the map. It fits one window.
artboards.gains: Active islands read at once; counts show where work piles up before a worker says so; the tray holds the detail, so the map keeps few words; the toolbar puts filter, plane, zoom and the list in one place.
artboards.costs: Focused hides quiet islands, so a forgotten repository with queued work is only a line in the corner; the tray takes 304 points from the map; counts are two more marks per island to learn.

artboards.title: The working map: Everything, the planar portal selected
The working map: closer on Humans Not Robots
The map of territories
artboards.gains: The whole distributed Agora in one look, with the key always beside it; nothing is hidden, so nothing is missed.
artboards.costs: Every island weighs the same, active or quiet; no counts, so where work waits needs another page; no selection or zoom, so a busy island's labels crowd and its detail is a page away. Was preferred until 1f.

artboards.title: 1a on sol's plane
1a on terra's plane
The councils

artboards.title: The two squares
artboards.gains: Host-centred: each Mac's Agora and the portal between them, with what needs a look and what was just said.
artboards.costs: Hides territories and islands, which Kris's vision puts first; treats hosts as places, not crews.

artboards.title: By Mac
artboards.why: Rows stay where Kris learnt them (by Mac, territory, work id), listening and queries read across each row, and the address book is one search away in the same view.
artboards.gains: Stable order; every fact about an agent on one row; the selected agent's detail below without leaving the page.
artboards.costs: Finding who covers a focus needs the search box; an agent with many focus areas wraps.

artboards.title: By focus: the address book
artboards.gains: Routing by focus is the primary act; shared focus areas and their primary owner show at once.
artboards.costs: An agent appears on several rows; listening and queries are per focus, not per agent; weak for "is everyone here?".

artboards.title: ki.prj.agora
artboards.why: One page holds everything needed to act on one agent, with the single brass action for what waits on Kris.
artboards.gains: Complete; the listening bars make a lapse obvious.
artboards.costs: Long for an agent with many queries; the bars need a legend.

artboards.title: One record, newest first
artboards.why: One record with a layer column and filters keeps the order of events, which matters when a push, a call and a reply follow one another across the portal.
artboards.gains: Time order is kept across layers; filters narrow to Git or Agora, one Mac or both.
artboards.costs: Busy hours make it long; the layer is a column, not a place.

artboards.title: By layer
artboards.gains: Teaches the two layers: what was written to the record and what was only said.
artboards.costs: Breaks the order of events across the two columns; a push and the call it causes sit apart.

artboards.title: Sent and heard
artboards.why: Pairs each broadcast with who heard it, and offers the one useful next step: ping the silent again.
artboards.gains: Answers "did everyone take the Away?" directly.
artboards.costs: Received broadcasts from terra need their own section below.

artboards.title: By agent
artboards.why: Kris answers a query in its agent's thread, so grouping by agent matches where the answer goes; oldest first within each keeps the longest-waiting at the top.
artboards.gains: Matches how queries are answered; each agent's load is visible.
artboards.costs: The oldest query overall can sit under a later agent; switch to Oldest first to see it.

artboards.title: Oldest first, all together
artboards.gains: The longest wait is always at the top; good for a morning sweep.
artboards.costs: Jumps between agents row to row; related queries (all of SCHED-) scatter.

artboards.title: The two Macs and the portal
artboards.why: The same two squares as home, with each Mac and the portal as a small table of facts below it.
artboards.gains: Facts sit under the picture they belong to.
artboards.costs: Repeats the picture from home.

artboards.title: Not level, side by side
artboards.why: Both Macs side by side make a disagreement plain, and showing only what is not level keeps the page short.

artboards.title: ki.prj.agora · messages.md
